title: Al-Quddus, the Most Pure
hook: the Most Pure, beyond every flaw, and a bucket of water poured in the mosque instead of shouting
tomorrow: why greet a total stranger with a name of God?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Malik: the King, and everything in our hands on loan. His kingdom. Today, what it means for a King to have no flaw at all.

A full glass tips across a nice dinner table, and every head turns to whoever knocked it. Now the mosque in Medina. A Bedouin, a man from the desert, walks in, goes to a corner, and relieves himself right there. People leap up, shouting at him. And the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says: leave him alone. What would you do next?
screen: `EVERY HEAD TURNS.` → `A MAN FROM THE DESERT.` → `LEAVE HIM ALONE.`

segments.voice: He asked for a bucket of water to be poured over the spot. Bukhari records what he told the angry crowd, in paraphrase: you were sent to make things easy, not to make them hard. In Muslim's version, he then called the man over and explained, gently, that mosques aren't for this; they're for remembering Allah, for prayer and the Qur'an. The place got clean, and the man kept his dignity. That answers yesterday's question from the ground up. Al-Quddus, from the root q-d-s, is the Most Pure: beyond every flaw, free of anything unworthy. Pickthall's list in Surah al-Hashr calls Him the Holy One. Nothing in creation is pure like that. People spill, stain, and get things wrong; Al-Quddus never needs cleaning. So for people, purity is something done, again and again, with water and care, like that bucket. Not disgust at a mess. The clean-up, done without shaming anyone. Something to tell a friend tonight: when the mosque itself was soiled, the Prophet's first instruction was to stop the shouting.
screen: `A BUCKET OF WATER.` · `EASY, NOT HARD.` · `AL-QUDDUS NEVER NEEDS CLEANING.` · `PEOPLE CLEAN, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · then, large: `PURE.`

segments.voice: Pick one small thing within reach: your phone screen, your glasses, a mug. Clean it slowly, as if it belonged to someone you respect. For the sit, set it down and look at it, clear.
screen: `ONE SMALL THING.` · `CLEANED SLOWLY.` · `LOOK AT IT, CLEAR.`

segments.voice: Al-Quddus: the Most Pure, the Holy One, beyond every flaw. People are cleaned again and again; He never needs it.
One word to carry: pure, the kind of clean that leaves everyone their dignity. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: found my first prayer mat from like age seven under the bed. it's gross. trash it or wash it?
options: Wash it, gently, by hand. Clean things up; don't throw out what matters.
Trash it. Once a mat gets that dirty, it can't be used to pray on.
Leave it. A prayer mat is already holy, so the dirt doesn't count.
chat.meaning: For people, purity is something done again and again, with water and care, like the Prophet's bucket. Clean it; keep what matters.
